body: Removing `ifNull(sample_weight, 1)` is a correctness regression. `sum()` skips NULLs, so any error event with no `sample_weight` (events ingested before sampling was turned on, SDKs that don't send a client sample rate, or projects added to the allowlist mid-window) now counts as 0 instead of 1. Counts come out too low, and a bucket where every weight is NULL returns NULL, and `toInt64(NULL)` is not a valid count. Keep the `ifNull(..., 1)` fallback.

`upsampled_count()` is aliased as `count` and replaces `count()`, but its `default_result_type` changed from `integer` to `number`. The meta the frontend receives for the `count` field changes type, so it can be formatted differently from a regular `count()` (e.g. shown as a float). Keep this as `integer`.

Using Python `hash()` of the project tuple as the cache key risks collisions: two different project sets can hash to the same value and read each other's eligibility, and a collision is never detected. The shared cache is also read by processes that may run different Python builds. Build the key from the sorted IDs themselves (joined, or a stable digest like md5/sha1).

This caches a single `options.get` lookup, which is already served from an in-memory/local options cache, so the gain is small. The cost is up to 60s of stale results after the allowlist changes, and nothing is wired to invalidate the entry. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called. It also only clears the entry for one exact (org, project set) key, while an allowlist change affects every cached combination of project IDs that includes the changed project, and those keys can't be listed. Callers can't use it to invalidate correctly. Consider dropping the cache or keying it on the allowlist's version.

Behaviour change from ANY to ALL: a query over several projects where only some are allowlisted is no longer upsampled at all. Allowlisted projects in a multi-project query (e.g. "My Projects" or all projects) now show raw sampled counts, while the same project viewed on its own shows upsampled counts. Totals are inconsistent across views, and if all-projects queries pass an empty/implicit project list, upsampling may effectively never apply. Confirm this is intended; the old ANY semantics relied on `ifNull(sample_weight, 1)` to handle non-sampled projects correctly.

This docstring says the allowlist is read fresh on every call "to ensure we always have the latest configuration state". The only caller now wraps it in a 60s cache, so the comment contradicts actual behaviour. The `organization` parameter is also unused.

Only `count()` is transformed now. The `eps()`/`epm()` → `upsampled_eps()`/`upsampled_epm()` mappings (and those SnQL functions) were removed. In the same chart, `count()` is upsampled while `eps()`/`epm()` stay raw sampled rates, so the series disagree. The `sample_count()`/`sample_*` inverse mapping and the result-key conversion (`convert_fields_for_upsampling`) were removed too, so clients can no longer ask for the raw sampled count.

The `if "timestamp" in raw_groupby: raise ParseError("Cannot group by timestamp")` validation was removed. A top-events request with `field=timestamp` now reaches the query builder and fails with a 500 or a malformed query instead of a clean 400. The PR also calls `self.get_field_list(...)` again in each branch instead of reusing `raw_groupby`.

The upsampling transform is applied on the RPC path (spans/ourlogs). Those datasets have no `upsampled_count` function or `sample_weight` column, so if eligibility ever evaluates true here the query will fail. It happens to be guarded only because `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False for these datasets. The same transform is repeated in three branches; doing it once before branching (as before) is simpler and avoids this.
